                    ### Question
                    To maintain blood glucose levels even after glycogen stores have been depleted, the body, mainly the liver, is able to synthesize glucose in a process called gluconeogenesis. Which of the following reactions of gluconeogenesis requires an enzyme different from glycolysis?

                    ### Options
                    opa. 2-phosphoglycerate --> 3-phosphoglycerate
opb. Fructose 1,6-bisphosphate --> Fructose-6-phosphate
opc. Phosphoenolpyruvate --> 2-phosphoglycerate
opd. Dihydroxyacetone phosphate --> Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
ope. 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate --> Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In gluconeogenesis, the reaction converting fructose 1,6-bisphosphate to fructose-6-phosphate uses the enzyme fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase, distinct from the enzyme phosphofructokinase used in glycolysis for the reverse reaction. This difference in enzyme usage is crucial for bypassing the irreversible step in glycolysis, aligning with the biochemical consensus on metabolic pathway regulation.
